method.overindex: Replicates an/vis_cbsa.py exactly: rows of the CBSA table with numeric TOTAL; Salt Lake City UT + Provo-Orem UT + Ogden-Clearfield UT summed into one metro "Salt Lake City–Provo–Ogden UT" (67 rows -> 65 metros); island columns O‘AHU, MAUI (island, not Maui County), KAUA‘I, HAWAI‘I ISLAND; base(island) = sum of island arrivals over the 65 metros / sum of metro TOTALs; share = metro island arrivals / metro TOTAL; idx = share / base. "over" list = metros with island arrivals n >= 10,000 ranked by idx, top 10; "top" = top 10 by n.
method.japan_canada_overindex: Same formula applied to Table 23 regions / Table 25 provinces: idx = (group visitors to island / group visitors) / (sum over groups of island visitors / sum of group visitors). Bonus, not in vis_cbsa.py.

notes: TABLE NUMBERING CHANGED: in the 2025 workbook the CBSA-by-island table is TABLE 56 (TABLE 55 is now "2025 Domestic U.S. Air Visitor Length of Stay (in Days) by Island and State", a new table). an/vis_cbsa.py hard-codes sheet "TABLE 55"; run against the 2025 workbook it would hit the length-of-stay sheet and fail its Utah assert. Point it at "TABLE 56" for 2025. Tables 23 (Japan by region) and 25 (Canada by province) kept their numbers.

Arrivals in Table 56 are visitors on domestic (U.S. mainland-origin) transpacific flights, classified by residence ZIP to CBSA; island columns count visitors who visited each island, so they are not mutually exclusive (multi-island trips) and do not sum to TOTAL. Values are survey-weighted estimates (fractional in the workbook); rounded to whole visitors in the output.

Table 56 uses older OMB CBSA titles (e.g. "Denver-Aurora-Lakewood CO", "San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward CA", "Ogden-Clearfield UT", "Provo-Orem UT") while Table 21 uses 2023 titles (e.g. "Denver-Aurora-Centennial CO", "Ogden UT", "Provo-Orem-Lehi UT", "Salt Lake City-Murray UT"). Totals match between the tables to rounding.

The over-index base is the pooled island share across the 65 listed metros only, not all U.S. visitors; idx > 1 means a metro sends a larger share of its Hawaii visitors to that island than the listed-metro average.

Year-over-year swings at CBSA level are large in DBEDT's own figures (Table 57: Dallas-Fort Worth -38.5%, Phoenix -33.5%, Albuquerque -39.2%, Denver +36.1%, New York +30.2%); state-level Table 19 shows the same direction (Arizona -30.3%, Colorado +34.3%, Texas -17.3%). Treat single-year CBSA idx moves as noisy survey estimates.

Japan Table 23 covers Japan MMA visitors on INTERNATIONAL flights only; the nine regions sum to the Table 22 "on international flights" total (743,614), not the Japan total (749,596). Okinawa, Shikoku, Hokkaido, Chugoku, Tohoku counts are small; islands other than O‘ahu have very small Japanese counts, so neighbor-island idx for small regions is unstable. Moloka‘i/Lāna‘i flagged by DBEDT as small samples.

Canada Table 25 covers ALL Canada MMA air visitors (both flight types): the twelve provinces/territories sum to the Visitors column and the Table 24 total (389,241). Nunavut is not listed. Small-sample provinces/territories (NWT, PEI, Yukon, Newfoundland, New Brunswick) produce unstable ratios.
Market Penetration (Table 21) = arrivals per 1,000 metro population as published by DBEDT (population column in thousands).
No owner rolls or personal data are involved; all figures are published aggregates.
